In mathematics, a '''Borel isomorphism''' is a [[measurable function|measurable]] [[bijective]] function between two [[standard Borel space]]s. By [[analytic set | Souslin's theorem]] in standard Borel spaces (which says that a set that is both [[Analytic set|analytic]] and [[coanalytic]] is necessarily Borel), the [[inverse function|inverse]] of any such measurable bijective function is also measurable. Borel isomorphisms are closed under composition and under taking of inverses. The set of Borel isomorphisms from a space to itself clearly forms a [[group (mathematics)|group]] under composition. Borel isomorphisms on standard Borel spaces are analogous to [[homeomorphism]]s on [[topological space]]s: both are bijective and closed under composition, and a homeomorphism and its inverse are both [[Continuity (topology)|continuous]], instead of both being only Borel measurable.

== Borel space ==
A [[measurable space]] that is Borel isomorphic to a [[measurable set|measurable]] subset of the [[real number]]s is called a Borel space.<ref name="Kallenberg15" />
